newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Small business needs lower rates-Australia PM.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Small business needs lower rates-Australia PM.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Sunday he would like to see more of the benefits of the three interest rate cuts by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) last year passed on to small business.

"They have had three interest rate cuts, although I would like to see more of the interest rate cuts passed on by the banks to small business," Howard said in a television interview on Channel Nine's Sunday programme.
"I think they (banks) are lagging a bit there," Howard said. He cited a strong small business sector as being an important factor in lowering Australia's unemployment rate.

"You will only get unemployment down if you have sustainably higher economic growth and if you remove the impediments in areas such as the labour market and if you give a fresh injection of life into small business," Howard said.
The Australian Bureau of Statistics is to release January's employment data on Thursday, with most economists forecasting no change from December's unemployment rate of 8.6 percent.
The RBA cut rates three times in the second half of 1996, reducing the official cash rate by 150 basis points to its current level of 6.0 percent.
